title: Ageing Populations and the Ethics of Care Technology
text:
Populations in many countries are ageing, and the proportion of citizens requiring long-term care is rising steadily. Robotic assistants and monitoring sensors are increasingly proposed as a remedy, promising to extend independent living while easing pressure on overstretched staff. Yet such devices raise questions about dignity, since being watched constantly can feel like a loss of autonomy.

The ethical stakes lie less in the technology itself than in the arrangements surrounding it. A sensor that alerts a nurse to a fall may be welcome, whereas one that records every movement for an insurer is not. Consequently, many gerontologists insist that older people be consulted at every stage, so that devices serve their preferences rather than the convenience of institutions.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what are robotic assistants and sensors proposed to do?
options: Extend independent living while easing pressure on staff
Reduce the number of citizens in the country

questions.text: What does the second paragraph say makes a sensor unwelcome?
options: Alerting a nurse to a fall
Recording every movement for an insurer
Being manufactured in a foreign country

questions.text: What does the passage imply about the arrangements surrounding a technology?
options: They are irrelevant to its ethical impact
They can matter more than the technology itself
They are always designed by older people

questions.text: Why do gerontologists insist on consulting older people?
options: So that devices serve their preferences rather than institutional convenience
So that older people can avoid all technology
So that insurers can set lower prices
So that staff can be replaced

vocabulary.definition: the quality of being worthy of respect
the ability to make one's own decisions and live by them
specialists who study ageing and the care of older people
organisations established to provide services or pursue public purposes

paragraph_translations: تشيخ الشعوب في دول كثيرة، وتتزايد باطراد نسبة المواطنين الذين يحتاجون إلى رعاية طويلة الأمد. ويُقترح بشكل متزايد استخدام المساعدين الروبوتيين وأجهزة الاستشعار كحل، إذ تعد بإطالة فترة العيش المستقل مع تخفيف الضغط عن الكوادر المرهقة. غير أن هذه الأجهزة تثير أسئلة حول الكرامة، لأن المراقبة المستمرة قد تبدو فقدانًا للاستقلالية.

تكمن المخاطر الأخلاقية في الترتيبات المحيطة بالتكنولوجيا أكثر منها في التكنولوجيا نفسها. فجهاز ينبه الممرضة عند سقوط أحد المرضى قد يكون مرحبًا به، بينما لا يكون كذلك جهاز يسجل كل حركة لصالح شركة التأمين. لذلك يصر كثير من علماء الشيخوخة على استشارة كبار السن في كل مرحلة، حتى تخدم الأجهزة تفضيلاتهم لا راحة المؤسسات.
